ideas.title: One stomp bounces the whole island
ideas.critique: This is round 2's drum skin again. What it adds is that every landing sets off a new ring, so the chain spreads by itself instead of being staged, and that is the strongest pitch this round. The domino film already showed a self-spreading chain tracked by the camera. If the rings are a few centimetres high and the throws look like hops, it shrinks to a wobbly floor.

ideas.title: Popcorn chicken
ideas.critique: This is the third telling of popcorn meadow. The spreading pop front is close to the domino chain and to the stomp idea next to it, so the self-spreading chain is no longer new on its own. The parts that count are still the GPU spheres piling into a hill you can climb and the dare to stand longest, and the score rests on whether the pile looks solid.

ideas.title: Magnet hour
ideas.critique: This is another Lumi body trick that gathers things onto Lumi. It has the same shape as the jelly swallow and the island's gravity ring, with props flying at a centre and sticking. The chrome and brass suit is a fair tracer showcase, but the generated props will likely snap on stiffly, and friends pulling pieces off will be scripted.

ideas.title: Apple bowling
ideas.critique: Round things rolling down the slope already happened twice with the sun ball, and nobody reacted either time. The friends falling like pins and standing back up in a triangle will be canned animations. A score and ramming trees make it playable, but a bowling gag is easy to guess and is worth watching once.

ideas.title: The sea attacks the sandcastle
ideas.critique: Sand as a heightfield the waves really wear away is a real simulation, and defending the castle is a game with a clear end. The sand rule and the dunes already made sand pile and slump, though. Waves done as moving water you can block will likely be height bumps rather than water, so the film depends on the castle visibly melting.
